title: Advanced Programming
prerequisites: Introduction to Computing Systems and Programming
objectives:
The purpose of this course is to study the principles and methods (Polymorphism, Inheritance,
Program Samples, and other paradigms of programming) necessary to produce a computer
program with good-quality specifications. In this regard, after covering the top-down design
method to solve the problem, students will be introduced to the concepts and techniques of objectoriented programming as a tool for managing complexity in medium and large-scale applications.
Program performance, testing, and debugging are focused on throughout the course. An objectoriented programming language (such as C++) is used to teach these principles and methods, and
students are introduced to the concepts and techniques of object-oriented programming and
module-based object design, advanced concepts such as graphical user interface design.
syllabus:
Introduction: Program life cycle, the importance of programming, programming paradigms,
Objected orientation
Object-oriented programming: Description of Objects, Object recognition, Finding implantable
objects in problems, Objects connection, Object-oriented programming language, an Introduction
to C++ and its history
A review of a functional programming language (C++), Polymorphism, inheritance, program
samples
Class and Objects, encapsulation and abstract, C++ classes and their parts (private, public, and
protected), constructor and destructors, derived classes
Polymorphism, polymorphism importance, function polymorphism, operator polymorphism
Inheritance: introduction to inheritance, single and multiple inheritances
Templates: template importance, function templates, derived data type templates
Other programming paradigms: introduction to event-oriented and graphical programming,
windows programming, client-side programming
Program testing and documentation: the importance of testing and documentation, automatic
testing tools, in-line documentation, technical documentation, user manuals
textbooks:
1. Bjarne Stroustrup, "The C++ Programming Language", Addison Wesley, 2004.
2. Stanley B Lippman, "The C++ Primer", Addison Wesley, 2005.
3. Paul Deitel & Harvey Deitel, “C++ How to Program (Early Objects Version)”, Prentice Hall; 9
edition, 2013.
